c.tagline: An ancient cave-dwelling city carved into limestone ravines, among the oldest continuously inhabited settlements on Earth

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small cave-district shops

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; the Sassi districts are pedestrian-only in many areas

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The Sassi districts are compact but very hilly and stepped, best explored slowly on foot; comfortable shoes are essential

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main practical caution is uneven, steep stone paths at night

hood_landmark.Sasso Caveoso: San Pietro Caveoso church overlooking the ravine
hood_landmark.Sasso Barisano: The rock-cut churches and cave hotels of Sasso Barisano
hood_landmark.Civita: Matera Cathedral atop the Civita ridge
hood_landmark.Piano (Modern Town): Piazza Vittorio Veneto and the Palombaro Lungo cistern

hood_desc: The older, more atmospheric of the two cave districts, with rock-cut churches and sweeping ravine views; ideal for boutique cave-hotel stays.
The larger, more developed cave district with the highest concentration of cave hotels, restaurants, and shops.
The elevated ridge between the two Sassi, crowned by the Romanesque cathedral with panoramic views over both districts.
The modern city center beyond the Sassi, with everyday shops, the main square, and the underground cistern museum.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, as across Italy.

transit.sys: Ferrovie Appulo Lucane (FAL) local rail and Matera urban bus network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; tickets also sold at kiosks
transit.note: The Sassi districts are pedestrian-only in many areas; a car is unnecessary within the historic center

transport.air: Bari Karol Wojtyla Airport (BRI), about 1 hr away, is the main regional gateway
transport.train: FAL local rail connects Matera to Bari (about 1.5 hr)
transport.bus: Regional buses (Marino, Miccolis) connect to Bari, Naples, and Rome
transport.car: Well connected via the SS7 and SS99 roads; parking is available near the modern town, with the Sassi being car-free

airport.name: Bari Karol Wojtyla Airport
airport.transport: FAL train, shuttle bus, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture

landmarks: Sassi di Matera
A UNESCO-listed labyrinth of cave dwellings carved into a ravine over 9,000 years, among the world's oldest continuously inhabited settlements.
Matera Cathedral
A 13th-century Apulian-Romanesque cathedral crowning the Civita spur, its restored baroque interior and campanile presiding over both Sassi districts.
Casa Grotta di Vico Solitario
A faithfully furnished cave home showing how Sassi families lived with mule and hearth until the dramatic evacuations of the 1950s.
Palombaro Lungo
A cathedral-sized 19th-century cistern hollowed beneath Piazza Vittorio Veneto, its echoing chambers revealing Matera's ingenious ancient water system.
Madonna de Idris
A rock church fused into the pyramidal Monterrone crag, its frescoed cave interior and terrace views defining the Sasso Caveoso skyline.
Chiesa di San Pietro Caveoso
The cliff-edge church poised theatrically above the Gravina ravine, star of countless films and Matera's most dramatic photo location.
Parco della Murgia Materana (Belvedere Murgia Timone)
The canyon-rim park opposite the Sassi, scattered with rupestrian churches and delivering the definitive full-city panorama at dusk.
Crypt of Original Sin
Dubbed the Sistine Chapel of cave churches, this 8th-century sanctuary outside town glows with remarkably vivid Benedictine-era frescoes.
Piazza Vittorio Veneto
Matera's elegant main square, where evening passeggiata crowds gather beside sunken hypogea and balcony views plunging into the Sasso Barisano.
Castello Tramontano
An unfinished 16th-century Aragonese castle on the hill above town, its stout round towers recalling the hated count murdered by Matera's citizens.

train.note: No international trains, and Matera is famously not on the national network - Trenitalia does not serve it at all. The private narrow-gauge Ferrovie Appulo Lucane runs from Matera Centrale to Bari in about 1h40, with no Sunday service, which catches people out. For anywhere else in Italy you change onto Trenitalia (https://www.trenitalia.com) at Bari or take a coach.

bus.note: The coach is usually the better bet. Marino, Miccolis and FlixBus run direct services from Piazza Matteotti to Bari (about 1h15), Naples (4 hours), Rome and Taranto, including on Sundays when the train does not run. Buy FlixBus and Marino tickets online in advance; local Grassani buses cover the Basilicata towns.

ferry.note: Matera is inland in Basilicata, perched above the Gravina ravine, with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. The nearest crossings to Greece, Albania and Croatia sail from Bari, about 90 minutes away.

half.name: Alberobello
half.blurb: A Puglia village about an hour away known for over a thousand cone-roofed trulli stone houses in its old quarter.

half.name: Altamura
half.blurb: A Puglia town about forty minutes away known for its Frederick II-era cathedral and traditional PDO-certified bread.

half.name: Craco
half.blurb: An abandoned medieval hilltop town about forty minutes away, evacuated after a landslide and left standing as a ruin.
